To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the work extraction process is conditioned by correlations between the state of the memory and the state of the molecule, and that this process can be described as the destruction of correlations between these variables.

the entropy of the Demon’s information is generated by the Demon’s operations, not by the memory reset, and that this entropy can be extracted from the system by operations conditioned on the Demon’s memory, but only when the information is destroyed.

the work extracted from the Demon is the entropy of information lost during the memory expansion step of his operation cycle, and that this entropy is the difference between the entropy of information in the memory at the end of the expansion step, and the entropy of information that would have been lost had the memory been erased before the expansion step began.

the study of the thermodynamic properties of Maxwell’s Demon and the Szilard engine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Demon’s memory-engine correlations are dissipative, that the work extracted by the Demon from his memory is not available to the engine, and that the Demon’s work extraction is possible only because the memory-engine correlations are not destroyed unconditionally.

the Second Law of Thermodynamics is violated by Maxwell’s Demon only if the Demon is allowed to extract work unconditionally, and that, when the Demon is constrained to operate only conditionally on his memory contents, the Second Law is not violated.
, in this referential approach to physical information, the Second Law is upheld in the sense that no work can be generated by Maxwell’s Demon without the loss of information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a generalized quantum mechanical Maxwell’s Demon, the work extracted from the Demon during a cycle of operation, and its associated dissipation, is determined solely via the correlations lost between the memory and the confined molecule during expansion.

, while the Demon can extract work from the heat bath without violating the Second law, this work is not free, but rather must be paid for by dissipative processes that destroy memory-engine correlations.
the Demon’s memory must be conditioned on the state of the engine to extract work from it, and that the work extracted is proportional to the conditional entropy of the Demon’s information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when a memory-engine correlation is lost, the Demon must pay a price in terms of work extracted, or entropy generated, in order to achieve the decorrelation.
the Second Law of Thermodynamics is not required to understand the thermodynamics of Maxwell’s Demon.
the information that must be erased to enable work extraction in Maxwell’s Demon is not the information that is erased in memory reset, but rather the information lost in the expansion step.
